title: IPod
description: Line of portable media players by Apple (2001–2022)
wiki_lead:
The iPod is a discontinued series of portable media players and multi-purpose mobile devices that was designed and marketed by Apple from 2001 to 2022. The first version was released on November 10, 2001, 10 months after the Macintosh version of iTunes was released. Apple has sold an estimated 450 million iPods. Apple officially discontinued the iPod product line on May 10, 2022. The iPod is the longest-running product discontinued by Apple, with a total lifespan of over 20 years.
Some versions of the iPod can serve as external data storage devices, like other digital music players. Prior to macOS 10.15, Apple's iTunes software (and other alternative software) could be used to transfer music, photos, videos, games, contact information, e-mail settings, Web bookmarks, and calendars to the devices supporting these features from computers using certain versions of Apple macOS and Microsoft Windows operating systems.
Before the release of iOS 5, the iPod branding was used for the media player included with the iPhone and iPad, which was separated into apps named "Music" and "Videos" on the iPod Touch. As of iOS 10.2, the Videos app was incorporated into the modern Apple TV app. While the iPhone and iPad have essentially the same media player capabilities as the iPod line, they are generally treated as separate products. During the middle of 2010, iPhone sales overtook those of the iPod.

History

Portable MP3 players had existed since 1997; however, Apple found that existing digital music players were either "big and clunky" or "small and useless" with user interfaces that were "unbelievably awful". They also identified weaknesses in existing models' attempt to negotiate the trade-off between capacity and portability: flash memory-based players held too few songs, while the hard drive based models were too big and heavy. To address these deficits, the company decided to develop its own MP3 player.
At Apple CEO Steve Jobs' direction, hardware engineering chief Jon Rubinstein recruited Tony Fadell, a former employee of General Magic and Philips, who had a business idea to invent a better MP3 player and build a complementary music sales store. Fadell had previously developed the Philips Velo and Nino PDA before starting a company called Fuse Systems to build the new MP3 player, but RealNetworks, Sony and Philips had already passed on the project. Rubinstein had already discovered the Toshiba hard disk drive while meeting with an Apple supplier in Japan, ultimately purchasing the rights to it for Apple. Rubinstein had also already made substantial progress on development of other key hardware elements, including the device's screen and battery.
Fadell found support for his project with Apple Computer and was hired by Apple in 2001 as an independent contractor to work on the iPod project, then code-named project P-68. grok_lead: The iPod is a discontinued series of portable digital media players designed and marketed by Apple Inc. from its debut in 2001 until the line's phase-out in 2022. Introduced on October 23, 2001, the original model utilized a 5 GB hard disk drive to store up to 1,000 songs in MP3 format, paired with a mechanical scroll wheel for navigation and delivering 10 hours of continuous playback on a single charge, which distinguished it from prior MP3 players through superior capacity and user interface integration. Apple paired the hardware with iTunes software for seamless file management and later launched the iTunes Store in 2003, fostering a closed ecosystem that enabled legal digital music purchases at 99 cents per track, thereby addressing music industry concerns over file-sharing piracy by providing a viable alternative to physical CDs and unauthorized downloads. Over seven generations of the core iPod model, alongside variants like the Microdrive-based iPod mini (2004), flash-based iPod nano (2005), screenless iPod shuffle (2005), and touchscreen iPod touch (2007), the product line emphasized shrinking form factors, improved battery efficiency, and added features such as photo/video playback, FM radio, and app compatibility in later iterations. Apple sold over 100 million iPods by April 2007, with cumulative worldwide shipments exceeding 400 million units through 2014 amid peak annual sales of approximately 55 million in 2008, establishing the iPod as a dominant force in personal audio consumption and catalyzing the shift toward on-demand digital media ecosystems. While the iPod's hallmark innovations in hardware-software synergy drove its commercial success and cultural ubiquityâexemplified by the slogan "1,000 songs in your pocket"âits market share eroded post-2007 due to smartphones incorporating similar functionality, culminating in the discontinuation of the final iPod touch model on May 10, 2022, as mobile devices supplanted dedicated players.
